mind_map.central_node: The Kites: Childhood Imagination, Skyward Freedom, and Aerial Perspective
plot_summary_nodes: Stanza 1 > Flying Birds Comparison: Colorful kites fly high in the blustery sky, compared to bright 'coloured birds in the wind-whipped sky'.
Stanza 2 > Wish for Weightlessness: The child speaker wishes to become small and light as air to climb onto a kite's paper wings.
Stanza 3 > Riding the Wind: Imagines drifting gently on paper wings while listening to the songs sung by the wild wind.
Stanza 4 > Bird's-Eye View: Looking down from above to enjoy a panoramic view over green parks and city rooftops.
Stanza 5 > Ground Onlookers' Awe: People standing on the ground look up in wonder, wishing they were soaring in the air too.
character_arc_nodes: The Child Speaker: Imaginative dreamer whose creative mind transforms kite-flying into an airborne adventure.
theme_and_moral_nodes: Primary Theme > Boundless Childhood Imagination: Creative thought transforms simple paper toys into magical journeys.
Secondary Theme > Aerial Perspective & Freedom: Experiencing the world from a bird's-eye view.
Cultural Festival Link > International Kite Festival (Uttarayan): Celebrating kite flying traditions across Indian states.
Moral Lesson > Joy of Play: Simple outdoor games inspire wonder and community shared joy.
key_grammar_nodes: Grammar Rule > Subjunctive Wish Form: Expressing imaginary conditions using 'I wish I were' (e.g., 'I wish I were small and light as air').
Grammar Rule > Similes & Personification: Simile ('like coloured birds'); Personification ('songs that the wild wind sings').
Vocabulary > Wind-whipped (blustery), Rooftops (tops of buildings), Sail (float smoothly), Blustery (strong wind).
Visual & Kinetic Imagery: Depicting upward motion, color, and wind currents in verse.
